target_material: metal oxides (titanium, zirconium, hafnium, tantalum, niobium oxides)
summary: The study demonstrates the use of photoassisted atomic layer deposition (photo-ALD) to deposit metal oxides using volatile metal alkoxides as single-source precursors. The process employs photons in the ultraviolet and visible range to drive surface reactions, enabling area-selective deposition through shadow masking. The films exhibit high purity, and the study investigates the photolytic mechanism, showing that the effective wavelength range is 190–350 nm. The results highlight the potential of photo-ALD for low-temperature deposition of high-k dielectrics like HfO2 and ZrO2 with promising dielectric properties.
